notes: No parts were added or dropped from step 1.

The first circuit image is the authority. It shows the Pi header rotated 180°. The red lead goes to the rightmost top-row pin, which is pin 1 (3V3). The green lead goes to the second top-row pin, which is pin 7 (GPIO4, matching LightSensor(4)). The black lead goes to the second bottom-row pin, which is pin 6 (GND).
On the breadboard the red, green and black leads sit in row A of columns 1, 3 and 5, using the image's column labels (column 1 on the right).

The circuit is 3V3 → LDR → node (column 3, GPIO4) → capacitor + → capacitor − → GND. The LDR spans columns 1 and 3. The capacitor spans columns 3 (POS, the long leg, on the same strip as the LDR leg as the tutorial says) and 5 (NEG).
Each jumper lead has its female end (a) on the Pi header pin and its male end (b) in the breadboard.
The capacitor is modelled as capacitor-10uf with value=1uF, because the catalogue has no 1μF type.

The tutorial describes many other mini-projects (LED, button, buzzer, traffic lights, PIR, ultrasonic sensor, MCP3008, motors). Its circuit images show only this LDR circuit, so only it is built. The 3x330Ω and 470Ω resistors in the parts list belong to the other projects and are not used here.
